explanation: Cancel pairs of unequal entries. Because one string occurs more than half the time, this cancellation cannot remove all of its occurrences; the surviving candidate is the promised majority.
attribution: Original C# implementation written for EPI Practice from the displayed contract; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: Removing pairs of unequal entries cannot eliminate a strict majority: each removed majority occurrence is paired with a nonmajority occurrence. The balance counter performs that cancellation online, so the final candidate must be the guaranteed majority.
walkthrough: For ["oak","pine","oak","elm","oak"], the first oak cancels pine and the next oak cancels elm. The final oak survives; it also occurs in 3 of the 5 entries.
edgeCases: The contract guarantees a strict majority exists.
A candidate may change after the balance reaches zero.
A single-entry stream returns that entry.
